sets.name: Franklin's Virtues
sets.blurb: The rules Benjamin Franklin worked on one at a time, in his own words.

items.text: Eat not to dullness; drink not to elevation.
Speak not but what may benefit others or yourself; avoid trifling conversation.
Let all your things have their places; let each part of your business have its time.
Resolve to perform what you ought; perform without fail what you resolve.
Make no expense but to do good to others or yourself; i. e., waste nothing.
Lose no time; be always employ'd in something useful; cut off all unnecessary actions.
Use no hurtful deceit; think innocently and justly; and, if you speak, speak accordingly.
Wrong none by doing injuries, or omitting the benefits that are your duty.
Avoid extreams; forbear resenting injuries so much as you think they deserve.
Tolerate no uncleanliness in body, cloaths, or habitation.
Be not disturbed at trifles, or at accidents common or unavoidable.
Imitate Jesus and Socrates.
Even if I could conceive that I had compleatly overcome it, I should probably be proud of my humility.

sets.name: The Stoics
sets.blurb: Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius on what is yours to govern.

items.text: There are things which are within our power, and there are things which are beyond our power.
Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.
Demand not that events should happen as you wish; but wish them to happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.
Never say of anything, “I have lost it,” but, “I have restored it.”
If you would improve, be content to be thought foolish and dull with regard to externals.
Never proclaim yourself a philosopher, nor make much talk among the ignorant about your principles, but show them by actions.
How long, then, will you delay to demand of yourself the noblest improvements, and in no instance to transgress the judgments of reason?
Begin the morning by saying to thyself, I shall meet with the busybody, the ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious, unsocial.
The present is the only thing of which a man can be deprived.
For nowhere either with more quiet or more freedom from trouble does a man retire than into his own soul.
The universe is transformation: life is opinion.
Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years. Death hangs over thee. While thou livest, while it is in thy power, be good.
How much trouble he avoids who does not look to see what his neighbor says or does or thinks, but only to what he does himself.
Such as are thy habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of thy mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts.
The best way of avenging thyself is not to become like [the wrong-doer].
Very little indeed is necessary for living a happy life.
If thou art pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgment about it. And it is in thy power to wipe out this judgment now.
No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such.
If it is not right, do not do it: if it is not true, do not say it.

sets.name: Know Yourself
sets.blurb: Writers who looked hard at the mind, the self and the way we live.

items.text: Above all, don't lie to yourself. The man who lies to himself and listens to his own lie comes to such a pass that he cannot distinguish the truth within him, or around him, and so loses all respect for himself and for others.
Pain and suffering are always inevitable for a large intelligence and a deep heart.
I swear, gentlemen, that to be too conscious is an illness--a real thorough-going illness.
"I did that," says my memory. "I could not have done that," says my pride, and remains inexorable. Eventually--the memory yields.
He who fights with monsters should be careful lest he thereby become a monster. And if thou gaze long into an abyss, the abyss will also gaze into thee.
One must not avoid one's tests, although they constitute perhaps the most dangerous game one can play, and are in the end tests made only before ourselves.
For to be possessed of a vigorous mind is not enough; the prime requisite is rightly to apply it.
Those who travel very slowly may yet make far greater progress, provided they keep always to the straight road, than those who, while they run, forsake it.
My third maxim was to endeavor always to conquer myself rather than fortune, and change my desires rather than the order of the world.
The greatest thing in the world is for a man to know that he is his own.
We must reserve a backshop, wholly our own and entirely free, wherein to settle our true liberty, our principal solitude and retreat.
The thing in the world I am most afraid of is fear.

items.where: Of the inconstancy of our actions
items.text: There is as much difference betwixt us and ourselves as betwixt us and others.
I study myself more than any other subject; 'tis my metaphysic, my physic.
All the unhappiness of men arises from one single fact, that they cannot stay quietly in their own chamber.
So we never live, but we hope to live; and, as we are always preparing to be happy, it is inevitable we should never be so.
It is not from space that I must seek my dignity, but from the government of my thought.
To believe your own thought, to believe that what is true for you in your private heart is true for all men,--that is genius.
Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation.
The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.

items.where: Where I Lived, and What I Lived For
items.text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived.

items.where: Where I Lived, and What I Lived For
items.text: Simplify, simplify.

sets.name: Questions to Sit With
sets.blurb: Open questions written for Scales. Stay with one as long as it holds you.

items.text: What am I avoiding by staying busy?
What am I carrying that I could set down, and what would get lighter if I did?
What do I keep saying I'll do, and what is really stopping me?
Whose approval am I still working for?
What bothers me most in other people, and where do I do the same thing?
What would I do this week if no one would ever know?
Where am I telling people I'm fine when I'm not?
What do I actually want, apart from what I think I should want?
What story about myself am I tired of telling?
What did I believe five years ago that I no longer believe?
Which of my habits would I choose again if I were starting today?
What am I afraid would happen if I stopped?
Who do I become around the people I spend the most time with?
Where does my attention go when nothing is asking for it?
What would make today count, even if nothing else goes right?
Where am I waiting for certainty before I act?
What did I love doing that I stopped making time for?
What would I tell a friend in my position?
What good thing do I walk past every day without noticing?
What part of me do I work hardest to keep others from seeing?
What do I need to say to someone that I haven't said?
When did I last change my mind about something that mattered?
Am I collecting things, or becoming someone?
What am I postponing until later that belongs to now?
